content.user_title: Analyze Mass Spectrometry Data with matchms
content.value_statement: Mass spectrometry analysis can become inconsistent across imports, filters, and similarity scoring. This skill gives focused matchms guidance for reproducible metabolomics workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to import and export mzML, MGF, MSP, JSON, USI, and pickle spectra.
Guides metadata harmonization, peak filtering, quality checks, and chemical annotation filters.
Compares spectra with cosine, modified cosine, neutral loss, fingerprint, and metadata metrics.
Shows reproducible pipelines using SpectrumProcessor and batch workflow patterns.
Covers library matching, clustering preparation, ion mode handling, and export decisions.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples; it does not include the matchms Python package.
Chemical structure features may require optional dependencies such as RDKit.
Results depend on input spectra quality, metadata completeness, and chosen tolerance values.
Large datasets may need memory planning and batching outside the skill.

use_cases.title: Prepare spectral libraries
use_cases.description: Clean raw spectra, standardize metadata, and export curated libraries for downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Identify unknown compounds
use_cases.description: Compare query spectra against references with suitable similarity metrics and quality checks.

use_cases.title: Build reproducible pipelines
use_cases.description: Design batch workflows that import files, apply filters, score spectra, and record decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Import spectra
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for reading data files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to load an MGF file with matchms and inspect basic spectrum metadata. Include the key decisions I should verify.

prompt_templates.title: Clean spectra
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a matchms filtering workflow for noisy LC-MS/MS spectra. Explain the order of filters and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare libraries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced library matching with multiple metrics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow to compare unknown spectra against a reference library using cosine and modified cosine scoring. Include validation steps for top matches.

prompt_templates.title: Build a batch pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reproducible processing across many files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible matchms pipeline for batch imports, metadata repair, similarity scoring, and export. Include checkpoints for failed spectra and reporting.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks how to compare unknown spectra against an MGF library.
output: Recommended workflow: load query and reference spectra, apply default filters, normalize intensities, and score with ModifiedCosine.
Expected result: a ranked match list with similarity scores, matched peak counts, and review notes.

output_examples.input: A chemist needs to clean low quality spectra before annotation.
output: Recommended workflow: harmonize metadata, require precursor m/z, normalize peaks, remove precursor artifacts, and enforce minimum peak counts.
Expected result: a smaller set of spectra with clear rejection reasons and consistent metadata keys.

output_examples.input: A data engineer wants a reusable processing plan for many files.
output: Recommended workflow: define a SpectrumProcessor sequence, batch input files, save processed outputs, and log filter outcomes.
Expected result: reproducible exports plus a processing summary for each dataset.

best_practices: Normalize and filter spectra before similarity scoring so scores compare consistent peak sets.
Record tolerance values, filter order, and rejected spectrum counts for reproducibility.
Validate chemical annotations before fingerprint or structure-based comparisons.
anti_patterns: Do not score spectra before checking precursor metadata required by the chosen metric.
Do not overwrite original raw files with processed exports.
Do not treat high similarity scores as confirmed identities without metadata review.

faq.question: What is matchms used for?
faq.answer: matchms processes mass spectra, applies filters, harmonizes metadata, and calculates spectral similarity for metabolomics workflows.

faq.question: Which file formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers mzML, mzXML, MGF, MSP, JSON, USI references, and pickle workflows described in the skill files.

faq.question: Can it help choose a similarity metric?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains cosine, modified cosine, neutral loss, fingerprint, metadata, precursor mass, and parent mass matching.

faq.question: Does it run matchms automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to help users work with matchms.

faq.question: Do chemical annotation features need extra packages?
faq.answer: Some structure-based workflows may need optional chemistry dependencies, such as RDKit through the matchms chemistry extra.

faq.question: How should I handle failed spectra?
faq.answer: Check for None after filters, record rejection reasons, and review metadata quality before scoring or export.
